dublinCore.title: Completeness Score Calculator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Quality
Completeness Score
Metadata Quality
Required Fields
Weighted Average
dublinCore.description: Interactive calculator for metadata completeness. Students check off 40 metadata fields grouped by schema section and color coded as required, recommended, or optional. A gauge shows the weighted or unweighted completeness score with a rating and stars, bars break the score down by weight and by section, the formula is shown with the current numbers, and a recommendations panel lists the fields that reach the next target fastest.

learningObjectives: Calculate weighted and unweighted completeness scores for a metadata record
Explain why required fields change the weighted score more than optional fields
Choose the fields that raise a completeness score most efficiently
prerequisites: Knows the difference between required and optional metadata fields

controls.label: Metadata field checklist
controls.description: Forty checkboxes, one per metadata field, that mark the field as filled

controls.label: Minimal
controls.description: Load a record with only the seven required fields

controls.label: Good
controls.description: Load a record with all required and recommended fields and eight optional fields

controls.label: Excellent
controls.description: Load a record with all but three optional fields

controls.label: Calculate
controls.description: Replay the score from zero and highlight the formula

controls.label: Weighted or Unweighted
controls.description: Choose which completeness formula the gauge shows

model.description: Completeness as filled fields divided by possible fields, with optional weights of 3, 2, and 1 for required, recommended, and optional fields
equations: unweighted = fields populated / total possible fields x 100
weighted = sum(weight x filled) / sum(weight x total) x 100

instructionalStrategies: Compute the score by hand, then check it against the formula panel
Find the fewest fields that reach a target score

assessmentQuestions.question: A record has 5 of 7 required, 6 of 8 recommended, and 10 of 25 optional fields filled. What is its weighted completeness?
Why can a record be 100% complete and still be poor metadata?
